findings.title: Stabilise cancels gravity applied during the same tick
findings.claim: flyShip applies gravity to velocity before computing stabilise, allowing the assist to erase gravity's sideways contribution completely.
findings.evidence: plan L743-L752 updates velocity from gravity before removing sideways velocity; spec L125 explicitly says stabilise never cancels gravity. Evaluating the supplied code with DEFAULT_FLIGHT, position (1200, 0), zero velocity, heading 0 and released axes leaves both position and velocity unchanged after one tick.
findings.why: An idle ship can hover against gravity instead of falling. The existing stabilise tests disable gravity, so they cannot detect this contradiction.
findings.fix: Compute the stabilise correction from incoming velocity before adding gravity and edge increments, then apply drag and update position. Add a gravity-enabled regression proving that stabilise preserves the tick's gravitational acceleration.

findings.title: Mixed contacts resolve in a different body order from the spec
findings.claim: resolveContacts handles static contacts for both ships before resolving their moving contact. The spec requires static then moving contacts for each body in crew/enemy order. The plan discloses an asteroid-order change, but not this change.
findings.evidence: plan L908-L915 places shipShip after the complete ships loop; spec L74-L86 requires per-body static contacts followed by moving contacts. plan L38 only explains replacing broad-phase cell order with asteroid index order.
findings.why: Collision corrections do not commute. With an asteroid at (600, 0), radius 20, and stationary ships at (545, 0) and (580, 0), the supplied resolver ends at x=532.5 and x=572.5. It resolves the enemy's asteroid contact before the crew's ship contact, changing subsequent corrections and leaving the enemy overlapping that asteroid.
findings.fix: Resolve the crew's static contacts and ship–ship pair before the enemy's static contacts, preventing duplicate pair resolution. Add a mixed static/moving-contact test that asserts the specified sequence and resulting positions.

findings.title: The Engines-factor test never checks damaged turn rate
findings.claim: The test named 'scales thrust and turn' checks only velocity magnitude. Turn assertions elsewhere cover only undamaged Engines.
findings.evidence: plan L627-L633 asserts thrust magnitude without inspecting heading or headingAcc; plan L612-L618 tests turning with healthy rooms. spec L109 requires Engines damage to scale both thrust and turn.
findings.why: An in-memory mutation removing the Engines factor from plan L738 still passed all 31 planned test assertions.
findings.fix: For damage levels 0, 1 and 2, assert accumulated rotation over multiple ticks using heading plus headingAcc against TURN_STEPS_PER_TICK multiplied by elapsed ticks and the expected factor.
